name: Korrath Cardamom-Rose Stim Drops
description: Small hard-candy drops infused with a low-dose adenosine-antagonist compound derived from synth-botanical sources, delivering a clean 90-minute alertness window. The cardamom-rose flavor is a deliberate callback to traditional chai culture.
flavor_profile: Floral and spiced — rose at the top, warm cardamom through the middle, fading to a clean neutral finish as the stim compound activates
cultural_context: Popular among night-shift workers and students pulling extended study sessions; considered a 'soft' stim option compared to more aggressive augment-stack products, and socially acceptable in most Tier 2-3 workplaces.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 school bans Korrath Drops after a student uses them during BCI-assisted exams, raising questions about where stimulant candy ends and cognitive enhancement begins.
A reformulated batch has double the listed stim dose — whether it's a manufacturing error or deliberate adulteration is unclear.
A character relies on Korrath Drops to function after a botched BCI implant disrupts their natural sleep-wake cycle.
